system.name: TrainMover
system.one_liner: an interruption-resilient runtime that migrates ML training jobs with minimized downtime instead of restarting them

components.name: TrainMover
components.role: top timeline: splits migration into a background preparation phase and a brief switching phase

components.name: Stayers
components.role: machines that continue training normally throughout migration

components.name: Leaver
components.role: the machine being replaced, exits after the switching phase completes

components.name: Joiner
components.role: the replacement machine prepared in the background and switched in to take over the leaver's role

components.name: Preparation Phase
components.role: background phase where the joiner's training stack is prepared without affecting the foreground job

components.name: Switching Phase
components.role: brief phase where the joiner synchronizes to the latest training state and takes over the leaver

components.name: CCL Switchover
components.role: the communication-library switchover mechanism used during the switching phase

components.name: Parameter Transmission
components.role: transfer of training state from leaver to joiner during switching

components.name: Training Timeline
components.role: shared horizontal timeline comparing TrainMover against stop-reschedule-restart

components.name: Stop-reschedule-restart
components.role: bottom timeline: the baseline approach that stops, reschedules, and restarts training from checkpoint

components.name: Stop & Reschedule
components.role: baseline phase where training is stopped and machines are rescheduled

components.name: Restart
components.role: baseline phase where training resumes from a checkpoint after rescheduling

components.name: Checkpoint
components.role: saved training state loaded to restart training in the baseline approach

flows.what: joiner ready, foreground job finishes current iteration

content.key_idea: TrainMover overlaps a background preparation phase with ongoing training and uses a brief switching phase to hand off state directly between machines, achieving far less downtime than stopping, rescheduling, and restarting from checkpoint.
content.reading_order: Top row (TrainMover) read left to right across a shared training timeline through preparation and switching phases with minimized downtime; bottom row (stop-reschedule-restart) read the same way, showing a much longer stop/restart gap on the same timeline for comparison.

palette.used_for: red text/arrows/X marks highlighting the switching phase, CCL switchover, and failure/removal markers
light orange background shading the Preparation Phase region
light blue fill for Joiner boxes

style.stroke: ~0.3pt gray/black borders, dashed rounded rectangles grouping Stayers/Leaver/Joiner
style.font: Arial/Arial-Italic sans, 4.5-10.5pt, italic for phase labels
style.arrows: many thin curved/orthogonal arrows (68 heads) tracing machine roles and parameter transmission across the timeline

encoding.color_means: red highlights the switching phase, CCL switchover, and removed/failed machines; light orange marks the preparation phase; light blue marks joiner machines; gray marks unaffected stayers and the retired leaver
encoding.line_style_means: dashed rounded boxes group repeated machine roles (stayers, leaver, joiner); red X marks indicate a leaver/machine being removed from training
encoding.emphasis: a shared horizontal Training Timeline directly under both rows lets the reader visually compare TrainMover's short switching-phase downtime against the much longer stop/restart gap below, with a green 'Minimized Downtime' annotation calling out the difference
reusable_patterns: two stacked timelines sharing one time axis to contrast a new system's downtime against a baseline
color-coded machine roles (stayer/leaver/joiner) tracked consistently across phases

evidence: instead of long restarting (bottom), TrainMover (top) splits the migration into two phases
in the preparation phase, TrainMover prepares the joiners' training stack in the background
the system enters the switching phase and synchronizes each joiner to the latest training state

summary: This figure contrasts TrainMover with a stop-reschedule-restart baseline along a shared Training Timeline. The top row shows TrainMover: Stayers keep training normally while a Leaver is replaced by a Joiner, first prepared in a light-orange-shaded background Preparation Phase, then handed off during a brief red-highlighted Switching Phase via CCL Switchover and Parameter Transmission, after which the leaver exits and the joiner takes over its role - contributing only a short pause to the shared timeline. The bottom row shows the baseline: training stops entirely during Stop & Reschedule (with a leaver marked by a red X) and only resumes after a full Restart that reloads a Checkpoint, producing a much longer downtime segment on the same timeline. A green 'Minimized Downtime' annotation calls out the difference between the two approaches' pause lengths.
summary_zh: 该图对比TrainMover与停止-重调度-重启基线：TrainMover在共享训练时间轴上，后台准备阶段(浅橙)让新机器就绪后仅需短暂切换阶段(红色，含CCL切换与参数传输)即可替换旧机器；基线方案则需完全停止训练、重调度并从检查点重启，停机时间明显更长，绿色标注凸显TrainMover的停机最小化优势。
